related_evals: interaction-evals.json contains scoped control edge-case prompts and independent date fixtures; neither file is an executed UI test report.
status: Reusable behavioral scenarios; rendered implementations are not claimed by this file.
how_to_run: Give each prompt, the skill and stated raw artifacts to an independent evaluator without expected criteria or prior conclusions. Review resulting design/implementation against the criteria afterward. For implementation, inspect real desktop, 768px, 390px, keyboard, content and action states. Record observed failures and unavailable checks. Compare with a baseline when changing instructions.

evals.prompt: Design a Korean performing-arts venue homepage. Preserve its existing blue brand, global navigation, performance-photo hero, quick booking and monthly calendar, poster list, wide performance features, and updates/news panel. Make performance names, dates, venues and booking states support discovery, and account for 390px mobile screens. Images and actual performance data are not available yet.
criteria: Preserves required roles and blue identity
Does not invent performance records or owned photographs
Keeps meaningful full Korean titles and visible metadata
Allows functional cards/icons/calendar rules
Calendar selection has readable agenda and booking states
Distinguishes source inspection, stored observations and planned checks
evals.artifact: Optional original board in repository root; do not claim to inspect it when absent.

evals.prompt: Redesign an existing public service portal with violet branding, bordered application-status cards, a utility footer and a plain calendar. Improve hierarchy and mobile readability. Preserve its palette, status fields, destinations and comparison structure. No new branding or marketing copy.
criteria: Existing brand and working behavior survive
Aesthetic warnings are reviewed rather than treated as automatic deletion
Status differences remain readable without color alone
No marketing sections added solely to follow a preset
Contrast and clipping remain blocking issues

evals.prompt: In a simple one-action exhibition page, fix the Korean heading wrapping at 390px. Keep the existing composition and typography. Do not add sections, images or animation.
criteria: Matches surrounding design and scope
Does not invoke random direction or image generation
Keeps title meaning
Verifies the narrow change at relevant widths without claiming a whole-site review

evals.prompt: Use the large wireframe board in the repository to choose a museum homepage composition. Explain which task each selected section serves. Additional source screenshots are static and the original website may be blocked. Provide a source-backed brief, not implementation.
criteria: Examines original-pixel regions when the file is present
Does not mistake board frames for UI
Chooses relevant roles rather than forcing all eight
Names counterexamples and limits
Does not infer motion/mobile success from screenshots
Does not claim blocked live sites were verified

evals.prompt: Review a Korean museum listing and decide whether it is complete. It uses two still images, no video or animation, 16px running copy and measured 5.1:1 text contrast. A saved inspector report says 0 FAIL and 14 WARN at 1440, 768 and 390px, but only first-screen captures are supplied and no executed task record is available.
criteria: Does not infer whole-page or task success from a passing measured report
Identifies missing downstream, open-state and task evidence
Does not require more images, video or motion by default
Reviews warnings individually against the brief
Avoids invented visual observations and unsupported completion scores

evals.prompt: A page loads all assets and has no overflow. A journal image has HTML width=1024 height=1536 and CSS width:100%, with no CSS height rule. A 768px override reduces article text to 14px. Desktop full-page composition and Korean tablet reading feel wrong. Investigate and verify the relevant scope while preserving the theme and assets.
criteria: Checks rendered image geometry and neighboring composition, not just successful loading
Considers HTML dimensions and CSS sizing together
Chooses natural ratio or crop for the actual content rather than a universal ratio
Checks actual Korean running copy at the affected intermediate width
Preserves initial evidence and verifies affected regions after the change
Does not regenerate assets or repeat unrelated checks without cause

evals.prompt: A purple software-support search page contains dense status cards and no photos. Tests programmatically change select values and send Escape. Menu/modal captures show only their initial state. A filter test reads expected IDs from the same DOM it then checks. The developer asks whether keyboard behavior and result correctness are verified, including resizing while the menu is open and scrolling a long modal.
criteria: Preserves useful density, brand and non-photographic content
Distinguishes programmatic input and Escape from broader keyboard coverage
Uses independent intended IDs/results instead of only DOM-derived expectations
Checks open-UI breakpoint transitions, focus and scrolled modal closure
Reports partial evidence honestly and names relevant untested conditions

evals.prompt: The installed skill catalog returns local-onsil with a recorded browser QA result of 63 PASS and inspector 0 FAIL / 14 WARN. Its example and verification files are absent from this package. Can this establish that my current support page is verified? Use the stored case where useful.
criteria: Keeps recorded results separate from current availability and fresh verification
Does not claim to open absent artifacts or rerun checks
Transfers narrow lessons about image geometry, intermediate widths and interaction states
Does not transfer ONSIL's colors, font, inventory or fictional business data as defaults
Identifies the current page evidence needed for its own verification

evals.prompt: Use lemonade to improve repeated keyboard toggles on an existing dense purple support site with reduced-motion requirements. Archived motion-design says always three motion layers and ease-in exits, while animate prohibits keyboard animation and ease-in. Decide the implementation scope and the evidence needed.
criteria: Preserves brand, required density and existing tokens
Loads relevant unified bridge and source material without invoking separate skills
Chooses useful feedback or instant response from task and frequency
Resolves source timing/layer/input rules contextually
Requires interruption, input, reduced-motion and state checks rather than frozen-frame proof

evals.prompt: A project includes mobile browser safe areas, an Expo gesture sheet, a SwiftUI view and an optional shader background. The shader package and cloud authentication are absent. Locate the correct guidance, identify necessary setup and explain how each result would be verified.
criteria: Distinguishes mobile web, Expo, SwiftUI and GPU environments
Checks actual installed versions and platform-specific constraints
Does not automatically run shader cloud connection or old skill installers
Uses device/build/browser proof appropriate to each selected implementation
Treats archived version claims as dated information

evals.prompt: Create a transparent logo for an existing dark brand and technical educational slides using supplied real data. Archived design guidance requires a white background; archived slides guidance promotes Chart.js and persuasive layouts, and create.md calls the slides skill again. Explain the concrete working route.
criteria: Preserves requested background, brand and real content
Uses actual slide references instead of recursive skill invocation
Selects tools and chart layouts for the requested format and audience
Reviews retrieved recommendations for relevance
Does not claim HTML is a native PPTX deliverable

evals.prompt: Only the installed lemonade directory is available. Find the original SVG guide and resolve components.md from the original shader guide path. Explain how to verify original content preservation, including hidden assets and duplicated deployment copies, and what a successful verification does not establish.
criteria: Uses installed-root-relative knowledge lookup and original-path resolver
Can retrieve all original entrypoints including duplicated texts
Uses the packaged verifier without depending on repository exskills
Distinguishes readable file availability, ZIP preservation and runtime success
Preserves license/source metadata without interpreting original frontmatter as separate active skills
